investigation.claim: A DELETE request establishes a tunnel to a server under the June 2022 HTTP standard used worldwide.

assertion.text: A DELETE request establishes a tunnel to a server under the June 2022 HTTP standard used worldwide.

analysis.reason: Direct factual lookup of DELETE request function under HTTP standards.

result.scope_note: HTTP standards are developed through IETF processes; no 'June 2022 HTTP standard' is documented as a globally adopted standard. The claim conflates DELETE semantics (resource deletion) with tunnel establishment, which is not a standard function of the DELETE method. The phrase 'used worldwide' implies universal adoption, which is unverifiable for any specific HTTP standard version.

assessment.rationale: Spans 234-236 define a tunnel as a blind relay that forwards messages without changing them. A DELETE request is a client request type; the spans do not state it establishes a tunnel. No support for c1.

excerpts.text: A "tunnel" acts as a blind relay between two connections without changing the messages. Once active, a tunnel is not considered a party to the HTTP communication, though the tunnel might have been initiated by an HTTP request. A tunnel ceases to exist when both ends of the relayed connection are closed.
